title: Shulgin's Ten Essential Oils and the Ten Essential Amphetamines
status_of_the_whole_series: HYPOTHETICAL as a human in vivo conversion. Shulgin's wording is 'in theory' / 'in principle': adding ammonia across the allyl side chain of each oil would, on paper, give the corresponding amphetamine. No human in vivo amination of an allylbenzene to an amphetamine has been demonstrated.
what_is_actually_documented: Allylbenzenes fed to animals yield tertiary aminopropiophenone alkaloids - dimethylamine, piperidine and pyrrolidine types - detected in urine by GLC/CIMS, NOT amphetamines (Peele & Oswald, PMID 870079). Propenylbenzenes (anethole, alpha/beta-asarone, isoeugenol, isosafrole) form no such alkaloid metabolites at all. The only amphetamine-adjacent experimental claim in the series is the rabbit-liver myristicin to MMDA report Shulgin himself cites, and the repo's own knowledge file concedes the products were most likely aminopropiophenones.

pairs.status: hypothetical; the rabbit-liver report is the only experimental hook in the series

pairs.oil_note: Shulgin names 'asarone'. The common calamus isomers alpha- and beta-asarone are PROPENYL and form no alkaloid metabolites; only the rare ALLYL isomer gamma-asarone (euasarone, sekishone) fits the series.
